evidence: All three scored dimensions are mode="batched" with aggregation="weighted_mean" (scored/{functional,polish,visual}/judge.toml lines 3 and [scoring]); both gates are aggregation="all_pass" and exempt. Each scored prompt carries explicit independence + continue wording after its gate: functional/prompt.md:13 'Once it succeeds, score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures and keep successful observations. A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles. When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job of your own if that is possible without the broken feature'; functional/prompt.md:7 'give that criterion its lowest score ... and move on'; functional/prompt.md:23 'Never deduct one observed defect in more than one row.' polish/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise judge each criterion independently and continue after failures.' and :18 'Preserve every completed independent observation.' visual/prompt.md:12 'Otherwise grade every criterion independently with its five anchors and continue after failures.', :14 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row.', :18 'Preserve every completed independent observation.' A case-insensitive grep of all scored prompts, app_context.md and scored judge.toml for stop|first fail|halt|abort|all-or-nothing found no stop-at-first-failure instruction (the only 'abort' is polish hro_pol_failed_send's request-abort test step; the template's 'Fail fast ... stop and fail that criterion, then continue the rest' was removed, not replaced by a global stop). The only all-or-nothing rules are the in-dimension global browser gate (functional :13, polish :12, visual :12), which the workbook/skill treat as the permitted gate (row 29), not a batched-criterion stop. Per-criterion zero clauses (polish hro_pol_live_board / hro_pol_live_thread 'If no update arrives within 15 seconds ... this row is 0') are scoped to that row only. Counterexample probes: (a) a plausible broken app with no live updates would lose hro_live_board, hro_msg_exchange, hro_unread_* and the two polish live rows but the prompts direct continued, independent scoring of e.g. hro_job_open, hro_reject_reason, hro_restart, so one miss cannot zero the rest; it cannot pass by this row's wording either. (b) A conforming app that hides refused controls or refuses in the UI before sending is not cascaded into failures: functional :23 directs replay of the captured request and states 'Whether a refused action is offered at all is the app's choice'; a failed setup (e.g. A never reaching Interview) is re-created on a new job per :13 rather than cascading. Runtime adherence by the configured judge is unmeasured: raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload ... and Oracle/target scores are absent', so whether glm-5.3-flashx actually continues after failures is NOT EXERCISED; that is a cross-cutting runtime gap owned by the workload/full-verifier rows, not a defect in this row's wording requirement, which is a prompt-text check (and owned deterministically by check-batched-independence-wording.py, not run here).
